chunks: From him, from Hammad and Safwan, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from his father, from Abu al-Tufayl: A group from Banu Najiyah, who used to live in al-Asyaf, claimed lineage in Quraysh. They were Christians, then accepted Islam, then turned back from Islam.

So Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام sent Ma'qil ibn Qays al-Tamimi, and we went out with him. When we reached the people, he set a signal between us and him and said: When I place my hand on my head, then strike them with weapons.
He came to them and said: What are you upon? A group came out and said: We are Christians; we do not know any religion better than our religion, so we remain upon it. He said: So he set them apart.
He said: Then another group among them said: We were Christians, then accepted Islam, and we are Muslims. We do not know any religion better than our religion, so we remain upon it.

And another group said: We were Christians, then accepted Islam, then came to know that there is no religion better than the religion we were formerly upon, so we returned to it. So he called them to Islam three times, but they refused, and then he placed his hand on his head.

He said: So he killed their fighting men and took their offspring captive. He said: Then he brought them to 'Ali عليه السلام, and Masqalah ibn Hubayrah bought them for one hundred thousand dirhams and set them free. He brought fifty thousand to 'Ali Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, but he refused to accept it.
He said: So he took it away and buried it in his house, then joined Mu'awiyah, may Allah curse him. He said: Then Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام destroyed his house and ratified their emancipation.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam 'Ali عليه السلام, the authority under whom the action took place
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, the religion which some had accepted and then left
key_terms.دَارَهُ: his house, which Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ordered destroyed
key_terms.ذَرَارِيَّهُمْ: their offspring or dependents, who were taken captive
key_terms.فَأَعْتَقَهُمْ: he set them free, referring to their emancipation
key_terms.مُقَاتِلِيهِمْ: their fighting men, those killed in the confrontation
key_terms.نَصَارَى: Christians, the prior religion of the group discussed

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith in Tahdhib al-Ahkam narrate about Banu Najiyah and the ruling applied to those who apostatized after accepting Islam?
ai.summary: This report recounts the case of a group from Banu Najiyah, some of whom remained Christian, some remained Muslim, and some apostatized after accepting Islam. It narrates the action taken under Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali عليه السلام against those who returned from Islam after being called back to it, and it also mentions the later purchase and emancipation of the captives.
